name: Six Senses Kyoto
positioning: Heian-inspired city hotel in Kyoto's Higashiyama district, opposite the Toyokuni Shrine
best_for: Culture-focused travelers who want to walk to Higashiyama temples and museums
Wellness travelers interested in Zen-inspired spa treatments and Zazen meditation

facts.text: The hotel is in the Higashiyama district, an easy walk from Myoho-in Temple, Kyoto National Museum and Sanjusangendo Buddhist Temple.
The hotel is opposite the 16th-century Toyokuni Shrine.
Rooms and suites offer a choice of views: the internal courtyard, the city, or the garden of Toyokuni Shrine.
Design touches are inspired by the Tale of Genji and ancient folklore.
The hotel is inspired by the art and cultural heritage of the Heian era.
Room design features artisanal craftsmanship and a touch of playfulness inspired by traditional folklore.
Six Senses Spa combines smart technology with traditional healing methods and Zen culture.
Sekki serves micro-seasonal dining rooted in the Eat With Six Senses ethos.
Guests can join a meditative Zazen session in a neighboring temple.
Earth Lab activities teach guests and locals about sustainability.
The hotel offers curated tours and exclusive experiences of Kyoto's cultural heritage.

highlights.text: Some rooms look over the garden of the 16th-century Toyokuni Shrine, directly opposite the hotel.
Design touches draw on the Tale of Genji, ancient folklore and the art of the Heian era.
Six Senses Spa pairs smart technology with traditional healing and Zen culture.
Guests can join a meditative Zazen session in a neighboring temple.

considerations.text: Views vary by room: the internal courtyard, the city, or the Toyokuni Shrine garden.
WhataHotel notes limited room inventory may require advance booking.
